questions.q: Monochromatic radiation of wavelength $\text{\lambda}$ is incident on a hydrogen sample in ground state. Hydrogen atoms absorb a fraction of light and subsequently emit radiation of six different wavelengths. Find the value of $\text{\lambda}$.
questions.solution:
As the hydrogen atoms emit radiation of six different wavelengths, some of them must have been excited to $\text{n} = 4$, The energy in $\text{n} = 4$ state is

${E}_{4} = \dfrac{{E}_{1}}{{4}^{2}} = - \dfrac{1 3 \cdot 6 \text{e} \text{V}}{1 6} = - 0 \cdot 8 5 \text{eV.}$

The energy needed to take a hydrogen atom from its ground state to $\text{n} = 4$ is

$\text{13}\text{.6 eV - 0}\text{.85 eV = 12}\text{.75 eV}$ .

The photons of the incident radiation should have $12.75\text{eV}$ of energy. So

$\dfrac{\text{hc}}{\lambda} = 1 2 \cdot 7 5 \text{eV}$

or , $\lambda = \dfrac{\text{hc}}{1 2 \cdot 7 5 \text{eV}}$

$= \dfrac{1 2 4 2 \text{eV} \text{nm}}{1 2 \cdot 7 5 \text{eV}}$

$\text{= 97}\text{.5 nm}$.

questions.q:
Which among the following expressions is the correct for the magnetic field at the site of the nucleus in a hydrogen atom due to the circular motion of the electron? Assume that the atom is in its ground state and the expressions are given in terms of the fundamental constants.
where $m$ = mass of an electron, $e$ = charge of an electron, $h$& = planck's constant)
questions.solution:
We have

& & & $\dfrac{\text{mv}2}{r} = \dfrac{\text{e}2}{4\pi{ε}_{0}r^{2}}$

$\text{or,}v^{2}\text{r} = \dfrac{\text{e}2}{4\pi{ε}_{0}\text{m}}$ & & & & & & ...(i)

From Bohr's quantization rule, in ground state,

$\text{vr} = \dfrac{h}{2\pi\text{m}} \cdot$ ...(ii)

From (i) and (ii),

$\text{v} = \dfrac{\text{e}2}{2{ε}_{0}\text{h}}$ ...(iii)

and $\text{r} = \dfrac{{ε}_{0}h^{2}}{\pi{me}^{2}}$ ...(iv)

As the electron moves along a circle, it crosses any point on the circle $\dfrac{v}{2\pi\text{r}}$ times per unit time. The charge crossing per unit time, that is the current, is $i$ = $\dfrac{ev}{2\pi\text{r}}$. The magnetic field at the centre due to this circular current is

& & $\text{B} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}\text{i}}{2\text{r}} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}\text{ev}}{4\pir^{2}}$

From (iii) and (iv),

$\text{B} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}\text{e}}{4\pi}\dfrac{\text{e}2}{2{ε}_{0}\text{h}} \times \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}m^{2}e^{4}}{{ε}_{0}^{2}h^{4}}$

$= \dfrac{{μ}_{0}e^{7}\pim^{2}}{8{ε}_{0}^{3}h^{5}}$

Let ground state energy (in eV) be E1

Then, from the given condition

${E}_{2n} - {E}_{1} = 204eV$

Or $\dfrac{{\text{E}}_{1}}{4 {\text{n}}^{2}} - {\text{E}}_{1} = \text{204 eV}$

Or ${\text{E}}_{1} \left(\dfrac{1}{4 {\text{n}}^{2}} - 1\right) = \text{204 eV}$ ... (i)

And E2n - En = 40. 8 eV

Or $\dfrac{{E}_{1}}{4{n}^{2}} - \dfrac{{E}_{1}}{{n}^{2}} = 40.8eV$

or${\text{E}}_{1} = \left(\dfrac{- 3}{4 {\text{n}}^{2}}\right) = \text{40.8 eV}$ .... (ii)

From Eqs. (i) and (ii),

$\dfrac{1 - \dfrac{1}{4 \text{n}}}{\dfrac{3}{4 {\text{n}}^{2}}} = 5$

Or $1 = \dfrac{1}{4 {\text{n}}^{2}} + \dfrac{1 5}{4 {\text{n}}^{2}}$

Or $\dfrac{4}{{\text{n}}^{2}} = 1$

or n = 2

From Eq. (ii),

${\text{E}}_{1} = - \dfrac{4}{3} {\text{n}}^{2} \left(\text{40.8}\right) \text{eV}$

$= - \dfrac{4}{3}{( 2 )}^{2}( 40.8 )eV$

or ${E}_{1} = - 217 . 6eV$

${E}_{1} = - ( 13 . 6 ) {Z}_{2}$

Therefore ${\text{Z}}^{2} = \dfrac{{\text{E}}_{1}}{- 1 3 \cdot 6} = \dfrac{- 2 1 7 - 6}{- 1 3 \cdot 6} = 1 6$

Therefore$Z = 4$

questions.q: An ${He}^{+}$ ion in the excited state, on the transition to the ground state, emits two photons in succession with wavelengths $108 . 5$ and $30 . 4nm$. What is the quantum number $n$ corresponding to the excited state of ${He}^{+}$ ion.
questions.solution:
The value of $hc = 1242nmeV$

∴ The energy of the first photon is

$\Delta {E ⁡}_{1} = \dfrac{\text{hc}}{{\lambda}_{1}} = \dfrac{1 2 4 2 n \text{m} \text{eV}}{1 0 8 \text{.} 5 n \text{m}} = 1 1 \text{.} 4 5 \text{eV}$

The energy of the second photon is

$\Delta {E ⁡}_{2} = \dfrac{\text{hc}}{{\lambda}_{2}} = \dfrac{1 2 4 2 n \text{m} \text{eV}}{3 0 \text{.} 4 n \text{m}} = 4 0 \text{.} 8 6 \text{eV}$

The total energy emitted by the electron during jumping from n2 to n1 is $\DeltaE = \Delta{E}_{1} + \Delta{E}_{2}$
$= ( 11 . 45 + 40 . 86 ) eV = 52 . 31eV$

or $\Delta E ⁡ = 1 3 \text{.} 6 {Z ⁡}^{2} \left(\dfrac{1}{{n}_{1}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{n}_{2}^{2}}\right) \text{eV}$

or $\Delta E ⁡ = 1 3 \text{.} 6 {Z ⁡}^{2} \left(\dfrac{1}{{n}_{1}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{n}_{}^{2}}\right) \text{eV}$

or $5 2 \text{.} 3 1 \text{eV} = 1 3 \text{.} 6 {Z ⁡}^{2} \left(\dfrac{1}{{n}_{1}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{n}_{}^{2}}\right) \text{eV}$

But the final state of the electron is the ground state

∴ ${n}_{1} = 1$

∴ $5 2 \text{.} 3 1 \text{eV} = 1 3 \text{.} 6 {Z ⁡}^{2} \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}}\right) \text{eV}$

or $\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}}\right) {\text{Z}}^{2} = \dfrac{5 2 \text{.} 3 1}{1 3 \text{.} 6}$

or $\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}}\right) {\text{Z}}^{2} = 3 \text{.} 8 5$

or $1 - \dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}} = \dfrac{3 \text{.} 8 5}{{2}^{2}} = \dfrac{3 \text{.} 8 5}{4} = 0 \text{.} 9 6 \left({\text{For He}}^{+} \text{Z} = 2\right)$

∴ $\dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}} = 1 - 0 \text{.} 9 6 = 0 \text{.} 0 4$

or ${n}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{0 \text{.} 0 4} = 2 5$

∴ $n = 5$
